ops.d: List every networkSecurityGroups in the subscription.
List the networkSecurityGroups in a resource group.
List every applicationSecurityGroups in the subscription.
List the applicationSecurityGroups in a resource group.

features.t: Network security groups (create, get, list, delete) over ARM

x: Flow logs are real Microsoft.Network/networkWatchers/{nw}/flowLogs resources (target NSG or vnet and storage account must exist, same region as the watcher, retention 0-365, version 1|2, one flow log per target, Traffic Analytics needs an existing workspace). Offline with netsim enforcement on (Docker backend; Azure VMs run on LXD/Multipass today, so only Docker-attached interfaces produce flows), real per-flow counters are written as v2 PT1H.json blobs (flow tuples with the matched DefaultRule_/UserRule_ name from the shared NSG evaluator) into insights-logs-networksecuritygroupflowevent of the configured storage account for NSG targets; delivery code is covered by unit tests with synthetic counters only (vnet-targeted flow logs, Nano and Traffic Analytics produce no data). Note that real Azure retired NSG flow logs for new creation in June 2025 in favour of virtual network flow logs, which this engine also accepts.

The 3 default rules per direction (AllowVNetInBound, AllowAzureLoadBalancerInBound, DenyAllInBound, AllowVNetOutBound, AllowInternetOutBound, DenyAllOutBound) are fixed display rows, not stored ARM resources — they can't be edited or deleted, matching the real portal.

features.t: Resource locks (Microsoft.Authorization/locks), scoped to this network security group
x: Lock create/list/delete are real Microsoft.Authorization/locks over ARM at resource, resource-group and subscription scope (CanNotDelete/ReadOnly, name and notes validated); this blade manages the locks scoped to this network security group only and has no scope switch. A resource-group or subscription lock really blocks writes and deletes of everything under it with 409 ScopeLocked (core/azure_arm_ext_core.py lock_conflict), but a lock set directly on a network security group is stored and listed only: it does not block writes or deletes of the network security group itself.

Only console/SDK-triggered mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill); severity/category filtering and the 7/30/90-day timespan picker are not modelled, and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity rather than the real signed-in principal.
Only the ARM Template tab is generated from the live resource; Bicep and Terraform export are not modelled.

Role assignments and role definitions are real ARM resources (Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments, roleDefinitions), and Check access / My access run the real wildcard + scope-inheritance + notActions + explicit-deny decision — all ENFORCED scoped to this network security group (plus its subscription/resource-group ancestors, matching real Azure's inherited-access view); Roles stays subscription-wide, which matches real Azure (built-in role definitions are listed tenant-wide too). Deny assignments and Classic administrators remain an honest gap — Microsoft Entra Privileged Identity Management and the legacy Azure Service Management administrator list are not modelled. Update: the Deny assignments list, Classic administrators (a read-only list of the subscription's account administrator, like the real API) and My access (the simulated signed-in principal, evaluated with checkAccess) are now real shared tabs (azure.common.*); the gap wording above predates them.

Support + Troubleshooting is the shared support-request panel (azure.common.support): requests are filed with Vyomi, not Microsoft. The 'Diagnose and solve problems' tiles (IP flow verify, Next hop, VM connectivity issue, Network configuration diagnostics — azure.nsgs.network_watcher) and Tasks (azure.nsgs.tasks) are built on real backends.

Lists the merged custom + default inbound/outbound rule sets from both the picked network interface's own network security group and its subnet's network security group, in priority order — the same two-NSG picture `az network nic show-effective-nsg` and the real portal's page show. It lists the rule set; it does not simulate a packet (that's IP flow verify, azure.nsgs.network_watcher). Scoped to network interfaces associated with this network security group directly or through their subnet.

features.t: Diagnose and solve problems: IP flow verify, Next hop, VM connectivity issue, Network configuration diagnostics (Network Watcher)
x: IP flow verify, Next hop, VM connectivity issue (Connection troubleshoot) and Network configuration diagnostics all answer from the shared netsim evaluator (core/netsim) — the same engine behind AWS Reachability Analyzer and GCP Connectivity Tests — scoped to a virtual machine's network interface in this subscription. Vyomi auto-provisions the regional NetworkWatcher_<location> resource the first time any of these tools run in a location, same as the real portal's 'Enable Network Watcher' behaviour. Network configuration diagnostics reports every network security group evaluated on the path (NIC and/or subnet) with its matched rule — the same picture `az network watcher run-configuration-diagnostic` and the real portal's result pane show — but, unlike the real multi-resource version, is scoped to one NIC rather than also reporting route-table/user-defined-route results. There is no standalone Network Watcher service console (browsing/deleting networkWatchers resources) yet, only these diagnostic tools reached from the NSG and Virtual network blades.

Packet captures are real Microsoft.Network/networkWatchers/{nw}/packetCaptures resources with the real lifecycle (PUT creates and starts, GET, list, stop, queryStatus, DELETE) and real validation (network watcher and target VM/scale set must exist in the same region, storage account or filePath required, timeLimitInSeconds 1-18000, totalBytesPerSession <= 1 GiB, <= 10 filters with TCP|UDP|Any and valid IP/port lists). Time and byte limits stop the capture (TimeExceeded / BytesExceeded) and a stopped or deleted capture writes a real libpcap .cap file to network-watcher-logs/subscriptions/.../virtualmachines/<vm>/<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/packetcapture_<time>.cap of the target storage account (readable through the blob data plane; Wireshark/tcpdump open it).

Each task (title, status, description) is a real tag on this network security group (hidden-task-<id>, JSON-encoded), written with the same ARM PUT the Tags page uses, so it survives a refresh and a tag written by another tool with that prefix shows up here too; it's hidden from the regular Tags editor, the same way real Azure hides its own internal tags. The cross-resource 'all tasks across every resource in the subscription' aggregate (a separate Azure Resource Graph query) is not built — only the per-resource list this blade shows.

features.t: Alerts, Diagnostic settings, Logs, NSG flow logs
x: Diagnostic settings (Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings) is a real ARM extension resource scoped to this network security group: logs/metrics are stored and validated exactly as the real resource requires, but never actually delivered to the configured destination (workspace, storage account or event hub) — there is no agent/telemetry pipeline. Alerts, Logs and NSG flow logs for network security groups remain an honest gap.

The Network interfaces and Subnets lists are real ARM reads (every Microsoft.Network/networkInterfaces and virtualNetworks/subnets resource in the subscription whose properties.networkSecurityGroup.id matches this network security group), so an association made via ARM/the CLI/another tool shows up here. The 'Associate' button now really works: it picks from every network interface/subnet in the subscription that has no network security group of its own yet (the same constraint the real portal's Associate dialog enforces) and sets its networkSecurityGroup over ARM.
